report:
Finding: Model B is tilted toward the culinary/recipe/restaurant domain.

Reasoning:
- Across deep layers (≈18–25) and positions 1–4—where the difference norm is largest—the logit-lens top tokens are consistently and densely food/cooking terms: “Cook,” “cooking,” “Cooking,” “Chef,” “Restaurant/restaurant,” “baking,” “Cake,” “kitchen/Kitchen,” “microwave,” “Professional/professional,” “cooked,” “Chef,” “Kitchen.” This pattern repeats across many layers and positions, indicating a coherent domain feature rather than noise.
- Mid layers already show related terms (“culinary,” “restaurant,” “hottest,” “blogs/blogging”), and later layers add consumer/food-blog flavored tokens (“Cake,” “Baked,” “microwave,” “Creative,” “Mail”), reinforcing a recipes/food-service/blog vibe.
- The difference norm concentrates in later layers and non-initial positions, consistent with a high-level topical/style shift rather than low-level lexical changes.

Conclusion: The evidence supports that Model B has been fine-tuned or biased toward culinary/recipe/restaurant content and style.
